incident_description:
We have a Weehoo brand child's bike trailer (model "iGo Turbo) that enables a child to be towed and/or pedal behind an adult bike. It was purchased on March 20, 2018 directly from https://rideweehoo.com The wheel of the trailer has been wobbling for about a week so I looked and attempted to tighten the wheel per the video instructions on their website, at which point the entire rear wheel drop out (on the "non drive" side, i.e. the side without the chain) snapped in half. My suspicion is that this frame area was already weakening/fatiguing as I had not really begun to tighten it when it failed with a cracking sound. The trailer has always been stored indoors in an insulated garage and ridden in fair/dry weather with our child. The trailer is rated to 80 lb cargo/child capacity, our child is nowhere close to this limit (currently under 55 lbs). We have used it in good weather to take our son to school and on short rides around town. We do not use it to "mountain bike" or on non-paved trails (i.e. we have only used this trailer as it was intended.) Fortunately no one was on the bike at the time and there were no injuries.

In looking at the frame design, it looks quite flawed/unsafe which is why I am making this report. Maybe by now the new models are better but there must be hundreds or thousands like our still in use as Weehoo is one of the only companies on the market I know of that make this kind of trailer and it is much loved by many parents. (Including us til last week!) On the drive (chain) side, the drop out and chain stay is quite strong and large. One the non-drive side, I have frankly never seen such a thin drop out or chain stay on a bike. Because it is typically covered up by the cargo panniers/bags, you don't normally see the rear stays so it is possible many people like myself never noticed it before. Even if the rear wheel is primarily being held by the drive side drop out and chain stay, typically bikes are made with two strong rear dropouts for a reason, due to the risk of the rear wheel detaching or hitting the frame. The non-drive chain stay is also the rear "cargo rack" on which the bike bags are attached, so this part of the frame is doing "double duty" as both bike frame and rack. Again, this is not a typical bike design because it makes for high loads on the frame. The cargo bikes I am familiar with that use that sort of design typically employ very large diameter, thick, overbuilt tubing to support the high demands placed on the frame in that situation.

I am not a bike builder but am a long time recreational and long distance cyclist with a fair amount of experience with bikes over the years. It could be that this design doesn't create the safety risk that I think it does, but even if the wheel stays in place despite the possibility of a crack/partial crack in the rear drop out, it still creates a risk that the cargo or the "cargo rack" part of the frame would loosen/twist and end up tangled in the rear wheel so again this just seems like a fairly concerning design. Again, I know that bike frames are inherently have a small potential of failure/fatigue, and at the drop outs particularly, but this design just seems unnecessarily risky.
justification: The incident involved a mechanical failure with no injuries reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood of such an occurrence is possible given the described design flaw and usage conditions.

incident_description:
I purchased a pair of BowFlex SelectTech 552 adjustable dumbbells for approximately $390 before April 23, 2024. While using the dumbbells for normal strength training exercises at home, I noticed the weight plates felt loose and unstable, which could have easily caused a serious injuryespecially when lifting overhead. I later learned that the product had been officially recalled due to this exact safety hazard, which has already caused multiple injuries to others, including concussions and broken bones.
Thankfully, I was not physically injured, but I feel that I was placed at real risk of harm due to the poor safety of this product. When I filed a claim through the official recall process, I was only offered a $90 store credit voucher, despite paying $390 for the dumbbells. To make matters worse, I was told I would have to return the product just to receive this minimal compensation.
I also learned that the original manufacturer, Nautilus Inc. (BowFlex), filed for bankruptcy in early 2024, and the assets were sold to Johnson Health Tech in a way that allowed them to profit from the BowFlex name without taking on any of the liability for these defective products. This feels incredibly unfair and deceptive. Consumers like me, who purchased in good faith, are being left behind with unsafe products and only offered a fraction of the value backif we return the productwhile the new owners wash their hands of responsibility.
I am reporting this because I believe this is a clear case of corporate irresponsibility and consumer exploitation. The product is unsafe, the recall is insufficient, and the handling of the bankruptcy and asset sale feels sleazy and deeply unethical. I hope this report helps bring attention to the issue and leads to better remedies for affected customers.
justification: The user was not injured but was at risk due to a defective product, which has caused injuries to others.

incident_description:
I represent an injured consumer who fractured several vertebra when he fell almost 20' from a tree stand on October 11, 2013 in [REDACTED].  The tree stand was secured to the tree by  Regal brand 1"x15' ratchet tie-downs imported from China by Service Tool Co, LLC, of New Iberia, Louisiana.  While these straps have a purported load of 1000#, the stitching in one of the straps failed when the consumer stepped on the tree stand.  The combined weight of the consumer and tree stand was approximately 240#.
Subsequent tensile testing of exemplar straps failed in the stitching at 344# and 116#.
It should be noted that the packaging did not even specify a maximum load, although it warned not to exceed 1/3 of the maximum load.
The consumer suffered severe back injuries and will likely have to undergo multiple-level fusion surgery in his back.
justification: The consumer suffered severe back injuries from the fall, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) given the product failure under normal use conditions.

I bought a Comodita Brava walker on Amazon in 2016. I really didn't use it that much until this year. It looked like new. While sitting on the seat on October 3, 2018 in Gulfport, Florida in a beach park under a gazebo, the plastic part of the walker suddenly sheared off and threw me on the ground. I had bloody elbow and knee. People helped me get up and notified the police who was nearby. He called the fire department. They wanted to transport me to ER. Instead I asked them to clean and wrap my wounds. Later that night I developed severe shoulder pain. Thankfully, there was no fracture. The force of hitting concrete floor, badly bruised my rotator cuff. I still have lingering pain. The walker is supposed to hold up to 300 pounds. I only 159 pounds. Reading a few one star comments about Comodita walkers, I realized that this is not an isolated incident and I felt I should report it.
I do have pictures of my injuries, broken walker, witnesses and a police case number.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries including bloody elbow and knee, severe shoulder pain, and a bruised rotator cuff, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to similar reports from other users suggesting this is not an isolated incident.

incident_description: I had a chance to inspect FOUR bicycle helmets Lazer G1 Mips, and ALL had faults that are safety concerns. I first purchased the helmet Lazer G1 Mips (size M, black) from an online vendor ( biketiresdirect.com). The received helmet had a safety issue as there was a cut in the foam with no ability to see how deep the cut was. After seeing the pictures, Lazer customer support told me to exchange it. The second helmet that I received had the same cut in the foam. I decided to get a refund from the vendor and order from Lazer directly. The third helmet I received was even more unsafe as the tightening mechanism (on this helmet called the rollsys system) did not work. An inexperienced user would have not known that it is unsafe to wear a helmet that way. Lazer told me to destroy it and sent me another helmet, now the fourth one. This one was even worse in terms of safety because the inner plastic structure that goes around the head was not fully attached to the remaining parts of the helmet. Upon closer inspection it turned out that a plastic triangular actor point that is normally located in the foam was completely missing in one part of the helmet. In other words, 100% construction error. Again, an inexperienced rider would have not noticed and would have worn a very unsafe helmet where the foam and outer shell were not even fully attached to the system that goes around the rider's head. In case of a crash, this helmet would have been barely better than not wearing a helmet at all.
justification: The description indicates multiple safety defects in bicycle helmets that could lead to injury in a crash, but no actual injury or death occurred.

After a long delay in shipping, I received a notification that the helmet has shipped.  The helmet was shipped from a small location in China.  When it arrived, it was CLEARLY not a Giro Aether.  Many of the safety features marketed on the site and were not in the helmet.  The helmet was cheap foam.

I did not use the product as it clearly did not meet DOT saftey standards.  I reported this to the company and was told not to communicate this in social media.  I asked the company for a refund and to stop selling this product.  They said they would investigate, but have continued to market this product.  

I explained that this is no different than selling a counterfeit baby seat.  It's a risk to any cyclist who buys this product thinking it will protect them in a crash.

incident_description:
I purchased a Rad Power Bikes RadWagon 4 cargo ebike for ~$2,000 in October 2021.  This bike is marketed by Rad Power Bikes specifically for having special, custom sized tires (22" -- a unique size for bicycles) made only for Rad Power Bikes through Vee Tire. These tires can only be obtained through Rad Power Bikes and these cannot even be obtained through Vee Tire. After riding the bike for less than 1,300 miles, the rear tire had a blowout. On closer inspection of the tire, I discovered that the sidewall had split (approximately 2") right at the bead, resulting in the inner tube bulging through the slit and cutting the inner tube on the sharp edge of the slit. When I searched for this problem on the internet, I was surprised to actually find out this problem is rather commonplace with these specific tires. I contacted Rad Power Bikes support (since the bike was still under warranty), but was told that Rad Power Bikes warranty does not cover tires. I argued that these are very proprietary tires that are obviously defective since it is happening to so many fellow RadWagon 4 bike owners. They never responded back and simply closed the trouble ticket in their system.  When further investigating this split, just pushing it with my finger cause the split to double in size. It was tearing/separating like a zipper being unzipped. Also, on closer inspection of my front wheel, the same problem is starting to happen at the bead of the front tire.  

I have seen recent posts in RadWagon 4 online forums where new 22" Vee tires are of a different design. Clearly Rad Power Bikes and Vee Tire are both aware of this issue or why would they change the tire design (when the tire is only used on this one model of bicycle)? 

Rad Power Bikes needs to accept responsibility for this problem and recall/replace these tires. This bicycle is specifically marketed for its unique tires, as well as specifically marketed for riding with children passengers. This bike is capable of achieving speeds of up to 25mph (even faster going downhill). If those tires were to fail while someone was riding this bike that fast (especially with children passengers), the end results could easily result in injury to include being life-threatening (or worse).  These tires need to be recalled and replaced immediately.
justification: The incident describes a tire blowout and potential for injury, but no actual injury is reported in the description.

incident_description:
On 9-22-2020 I purchased a Barnett DRT 385 crossbow from Dunham Sporting Goods.  I put it together per the instructions.  The Crank Cocking Device was already installed on the crossbow.
On 9-23-2020 I went to cock the crossbow using the crank cocking device.  I cranks the bow back to about 3/4 cocked, when the crank cocking device string broke.  This allowed the two hard plastic hooks that pull the bow string back to fly forward and into the top of my foot.  The two hooks caused puncture wounds to the top of my foot.  X-rays revealed no broken bones.  I have severe soft tissue damage the size of a baseball to the top of my foot.  Dr [REDACTED], Ankle and Foot Specialist has me wearing a compression sock to reduce the chance of a blood clog.  I have to wear a Support Boot and keep my foot elevated as much as possible.
There are several complaints on the internet of the crank cocking device string breaking while cocking.  One person reported that the hooks missed his foot, but hit and ground and then ricocheted up striking him in the forehead
The string might not break until the 3rd or 4th time cranking, but it will break.
I tried calling Barnett Crossbows.  No answer at Customer Service.  I stayed on hold for over an hour waiting, while I played a video game.  I tried emailing them.  No replies to my five (5) emails.  Again on9-25-2020 I called and waited on hold for over an hour.  Still no answer.  Why are they in hiding?  What other defective products do they have out in the market place?
justification: The incident resulted in injury (puncture wounds and soft tissue damage) and there are multiple reports of similar incidents, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
Text of Submitter's e-mail message dated September 29, 2015:

Subject: Formal complaint / recall required MotoTec 1600w Dirt Electric Skateboard DUAL MOTOR

I'm lucky to be alive writing this. Through walmart, I purchased the MotoTec 1600w Dirt Electric Skateboard DUAL MOTOR. After my 10th ride or so, I was riding down the street going 15/18 mph. I accidentally touched the top of the controller and hit the speed button. The wheels instantly locked up. You can imagine what happened next. I barrel rolled down the asphalt about 40ft. I have scrapes and road rash and internal bruises all over. I am an adventurous person and also an engineer. I know that these types of remotes need to have a failsafe in case buttons are accidentally or intentionally pressed. It should absolutely not lock up the wheels if I press ANY button. It needs to disable all buttons while the board is in motion. This is the worst safety oversight I have ever seen in a product. I am 35 years old. I cringe when I think of a kid using this, accidentally (or even intentionally) pressing a button and then possibly getting hit by a car. I very strongly urge you to stop selling and distributing this until this problem is fixed. You also need to notify those that have purchased it of this problem. This needs to happen immediately. Go ahead and test one, but if mine did it, others will do it too.
justification: The user suffered scrapes, road rash, and internal bruises from the incident, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
On Sunday, December 14th, 2014, my 4 year old son was riding his recently purchased MXR16 Raleigh bicycle with training wheels in Long Beach, California, at relatively slow speed under the supervision of his mother, a registered nurse, and father, an epidemiologist, on a relatively clean and fenced in paved recreation area at a local middle school.  The child was wearing a Bell helmet as well as Bell kneepads and elbow pads.  At approximately 1:00 pm under clear weather, my son slowly tipped over, just out of the reach of his father, and fell to his right onto the pavement while gripping the handles and remaining in a seated position.  He immediately let out a scream and began intensely crying.  As his father picked him up, he noticed a significant amount of blood emanating from the childs right pinky finger, which was amputated cross-sectionally from the left to the right side and was dangling from a sliver of skin.  The pinky finger of the right hand had become caught between the right handle of the handlebar and the pavement and the cylinder of the metal handlebar, under the weight of the bicycle and the 35 pound pre-schooler, had protruded from the rubberized handle.

The child was taken immediately to the closest ER at Long Beach Memorial Hospital, where the ED diagnosis was right hand fifth finger tip of the finger with near complete amputation approximately 3 mm segment no involvement of the MCP, PIP, DIP.  With tuft fracture.  The patients finger was cleaned, stabilized, x-rayed, immobilized with xeroform dressing, the patient given pain management mediation, and the patient was referred for a next day visit with a local hand and wrist specialist.

The next day, the hand and wrist specialist physician informed the patients mother that the amputation was not amenable to surgical intervention, prescribed antibiotics and analgesic medication, and advised to follow up with Kaiser Permanente, the patients health care system.  The patient is currently (12/27/14) being monitored by Kaiser Permanente as the fingertip tissue dies, dries, and falls off.
justification: The child suffered a near-complete amputation of the pinky finger, which constitutes a significant injury.

incident_description:
Bought a treadmill. It came with a magnetic key on a red string with a clip at the other end. The treadmill is not supposed to function unless the magnetic key is in place on the treadmill console. The clip is meant to be clipped to the user, with the idea of being that if the user falls or gets too far from the treadmill, it would pull the magnetic key away from the console which in turn would turn off the treadmill. The magnetic key portion is a small, red plastic piece with a small magnet glued inside an indentation. 
I was using my treadmill with the clip attached to my t-shirt, and I stumbled and took a step away from the treadmill. The magnetic safety key came apart in that the magnet stayed attached to the console of the treadmill while the plastic part attached to the string came away from the magnet. Thus, the treadmill did not turn off as it was supposed to in a situation like that; it continued to run just as normal. Since that incident, the treadmill will operate normally with just the magnet attached to the console, and without the safety magnetic switch attached in any way.
justification: The safety mechanism failed, posing a risk of injury if the user falls and the treadmill does not stop as intended.

incident_description:
My son and I were mountain biking when my son took a spill. The result was a skinned knee and elbow, a cut across the bridge of his nose (not bleeding), and a bloody nose from the left nostril. I was surprised about the cut & bloody nose since he was wearing a full face Demon Podium helmet with MIPS. I asked him if he hit a bush or rock, and he said no, just the ground. I checked his helmet and there were no dents or major scrapes, but the visor/peak was pushed below the front brim and couldn't be put back in place since it was wedged under the brim. Also, one of the gray visor bolts was ripped out and missing on the right side. After about 15min, he developed a headache, so we went to the ER where a cat scan confirmed a broken nose and mild concussion.  I  was dumbfounded about the broken nose, especially with a full face helmet. While inspecting the helmet, I slid my finger along the inside edge of the foam padding (typically rests against the forehead), and at the midline, I found a small depression. I checked my other son's helmet (never worn) and the forehead pad inner edge was smooth with no depressions. I had my son put his helmet on and the forehead pad depression aligns with the bridge of his nose. After confirming the chin strap was properly secured, I was able to rotate the helmet down resulting in the brim foam pad connecting with the bridge of his nose. It appears as he hit the ground, the visor took most of the force and since it was secured to the helmet, it rotated the helmet into my son's face.
After searching the internet, it seems this type of injury is common.  To improve the design, the helmet visor should be able to break-away during an impact.  This would prevent it from pivoting the helmet out of its proper position.
justification: The incident resulted in a broken nose and mild concussion, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The description notes that this type of injury is common, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description:
While riding Polaris Sportsman 500 down a steep descent, the machine suddenly experienced total brake failure.  This ATV is equipped with both a hand actuated brake which operates both front and rear brakes along with a foot actuated brake that operates rear brakes.  This machine was well maintained and both systems were checked and fully functional before vehicle was operated.  This machine is EXTREMELY DANGEROUS due to several design flaws including:

1- The machine has an automatic (CVT) transmission that does not have engine brakes and cannot be shifted or slowed by utilizing the engine or transmission; i.e. the brakes are the only way to stop or even slow this machine.

2- A single point of failure resulted in complete brake loss.  The hand brake has a completely separate brake fluid reservoir from the foot brake and both have separate hydraulic lines feeding the brakes.  However due to design flaws in this system, a single failure resulted in both the hand and foot brakes failing at the same time.

3- ATVs are designed to be ridden off-road in varied and sometimes steep terrain.  The design of this vehicle does not include any system redundancy to prevent catastrophic brake failure.  The failure of a single component resulted in an EXTREMELY DANGEROUS situation and complete inability to stop or even slow a 500 lb.+ ATV.

The design flaws inherent in this machine nearly cost me my life. I hope this information prevents this machine costing others their own.
justification: The incident describes a near-fatal situation due to design flaws, indicating high severity and likelihood of recurrence.

The clasp was still connected and the pressure from the chin strap was choking him.  Luckily my 5 year old recognized the distress and brought him to me as I was in a different area.  My wife is from [REDACTED] and she wanted me to file this report.  In Sweden they are required to have pressure release clasps on children's bike helmets.  She hopes that by filing this report that maybe the US will follow that thinking.
justification: The child was choking due to the helmet strap, indicating a potential injury, but no lasting harm was reported.

The respondents organization is claiming  a hazard because 3.5, (Suspended hazards), in the playground safety handbook.

Report Update:
NOTE: The respondent filed this report on behalf of the family involved in the incident.

5/28/2016: A 9 year-old child, after climbing down to the ground using a vertical pole type ladder from an elevated
circular slide platform at a children's playground, turned to run away from another child who was pursuing him
and hit his nose on a suspended metal pipe and sustained a nasal fracture with deformity & obstruction. The
children were playing a game of tag and the child at issue herein was being chased.

The child was taken by his parents directly to their medical provider and then quickly transported to the hospital.

The structure is an elevated circular platform, approximately six (6) feet above the ground. At one end it
has two (2) slides leading to the ground. Looking at the structure from a side view with the slides to the extreme
right end of the view, there is a conventional stairway from the ground to the elevated platform. About eight (8)
feet to the right of said stairway, there is a vertical pole type ladder from the ground to the elevated platform.
About two (2) feet to the right of said vertical pole type ladder there is a six (6) foot, six (6) inch diameter metal
pipe buried vertically into the ground at a location about four (4) feet away from the structure. Please see pictures
of the claimed suspended hazard at issue herein and attached hereto as EXHIBIT 1, side view picture A and
end view (slides) picture B.

Further, there is a four (4) foot long, two (2) inch diameter metal pipe that is suspended horizontally four
(4) feet above the ground, and which is connected between the structure and the abovementioned six (6) foot high,
six (6) inch diameter, free-standing metal pipe. Please see EXHIBIT 2, an annotated picture attached hereto
depicting the claimed defect at issue herein. This configuration creates a suspended component that is less than
the required seven (7) feet above the ground height minimum that is specified in the Public Playground Safety
Handbook published by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. Please see page 16, Section 3.5 -
Suspended Hazards, of said Safety Handbook attached hereto as EXHIBIT 3.

PLEASE TAKE NOTICE, that the law in New York State, General Business Law 399-dd specifies that public
playgrounds must comply with the guidelines issued by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. Please
see inquiry reply from New York State Department of Health to this office, attached hereto as EXHIBIT 4.

The respondent's organization is claiming a hazard because 3.5, (Suspended hazards) in the playground safety
handbook.

incident_description: My 22 year old daughter was using a Lime Electric Scooter in Old Town, Scottsdale AZ. The sidewalk took a sharp turn and the scooter was unable to stop to slow down to take the corner. As a result, she was thrown off the scooter and was knocked unconscious for over 10 minutes. She suffered severe head trauma as well as trauma to the lower back, chest, arm and face. She was taken by ambulance, unconscious to the closest trauma ER hospital. She suffered a double skull fracture and brain bleed and swelling to the head. She remained in the ICU for 4 days and was sent home. Upon returning home, she suffered extreme pain which was uncontrollable from non IV meds, from the brain bleed "feathering" out in tight areas of her brain, and went back to the ICU in hospital again. She lost a month of work, and is looking at a 120K hospital bill to date.
justification: The incident resulted in severe head trauma, skull fractures, and a brain bleed requiring ICU hospitalization, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description: My 11 year  old daughter (will be 12 Aug 26th) was playing with "The Human Slingshot" by VAT19 with two 12-year olds and one 13-year old of similar build. The product instructions state 4 players only. My daughter collided with another player and sustained a fractured and dislocated clavicle which the emergency room doctor stated would more than likely require surgery due to the severity of her injury. This product has no age limits on the instructions and is a very dangerous product for younger less coordinated children as the product obviously requires controlled coordination while being sling-shotted back and forth among three other players. In essence, this product is an accident waiting to happen. We did not own this product as we were visiting a friend's house when my daughter participated in this game.
justification: The incident resulted in a fractured and dislocated clavicle requiring surgery, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The description suggests the product is inherently dangerous for children, making such injuries likely (occurrence likelihood 4).
